# binpazer benchmark results

A ratio in parentheses is relative to the reference implementation.

## Run and environment

```text
mode                      full
timed runs per operation  5
reference                 C
cpu                       Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz
logical cores             4
memory                    15.7 GiB
os                        Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
kernel                    6.18.44-fc-v726
work dir filesystem       tmpfs
node                      v22.23.5
cc                        cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0
c++                       c++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0
go cli                    binpazer version dev (b5b25eff)
python                    Python 3.13.18
```

## How to reproduce

```sh
make -C bench
make -C bench prof
(cd go && go-toolchain)
(cd ts && ts0 build)
node bench/run.ts --profile --work-dir /mnt/cc-tmpfs/bpz-full
```

## Notes

- CPU time is user + sys of the whole process, including runtime start-up.
- Max RSS is the kernel's ru_maxrss for the process.
- Read, stream and find all read the file that the reference implementation wrote.
- Throughput is logical (decoded) bytes divided by the median wall time.
- Every write and read goes through the filesystem of the work directory. A RAM-backed one keeps the block device out of the numbers.
- Compressed file sizes can differ because encoder output is implementation-defined. Every implementation decodes every other implementation's file to the same result.
- For codec none and stored, the files that every implementation writes are byte-identical.

## Where the CPU time goes (self time, top functions)

Tools: C gprof, C++ gprof, Go pprof, TypeScript v8 cpu-prof, Python cProfile. A percentage is a share of the sampled CPU time. The profiled runs are separate runs from the timed ones. A fast operation is profiled several times and the samples are summed, because a sampler takes few samples from a short run.
